turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Morning, Dana. Got a minute? I need to walk you through the schema migration I just pushed.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Sure, but I thought we were holding off until after the audit. Did you run the test suite first?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Honestly? No. I was under pressure to get it done, so I deployed without running the tests. I know that's not ideal.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Not ideal? Sam, that's how regressions slip into production. What about a rollback plan?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: The migration could always be rolled back — I made sure of that. And I took a full snapshot before the migration, so we're covered.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: A snapshot is fine, but did you back up the old schema separately? You know, in case the snapshot gets corrupted?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: I didn't do a separate backup, no. But the snapshot is right there on the same storage cluster. Should be fine.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: I really hope you're right. Let's check the customer records after lunch.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Sam, we have a problem. The migration corrupted customer records — I'm seeing null fields and duplicated IDs across the board.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: What? That can't be. I took a full snapshot before the migration, so we can restore from that.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: We tried. The corruption spread to the backups — the snapshot itself is now garbage. It's going to take days to repair.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Days? That's a nightmare. I thought the snapshot was bulletproof.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: It wasn't. And because you didn't run the test suite, we didn't catch the regression until it hit production. This is exactly what I warned you about.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: You're right. I'm sorry. I need to fix this properly. I'm going to set up point-in-time recovery snapshots independent of the backup system — so if one fails, the other doesn't.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: That's a start. But we also need to make sure untested code never reaches production again. Can you set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Yes. I'll do that today. And I'll run the full test suite on the repair branch before we even think about deploying.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Good news — the repair finished overnight. Customer records are clean again. How's the CI gate working?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: It's live. No merge gets through without tests passing. Untested code never reaches production now — that part is solid.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Great. And the point-in-time recovery snapshots? Are those holding up?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: They're working, but I have to be honest — I was wrong about the full snapshot approach. Turns out that wasn't enough. The snapshot went stale by deploy time, because we had new writes coming in during the migration window.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: So what did you replace it with?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: We switched to continuous replication. Now every write is mirrored to a separate cluster in real time, so even if a migration goes sideways, we can roll back to the exact second before the change — not just a snapshot from hours earlier.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: That's a much better safety net. And it means the rollback is always possible, even mid-deploy.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Exactly. The old snapshot approach fell short because it was a single point in time. Continuous replication is the real fix.

turns.speaker: Dana
turns.text: Good. Let's document this and make sure the next migration follows the same pattern.
